memories.author: D03
memories.text:
74-year-old male with BPH presents for routine follow-up.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He reports mild nocturia twice nightly and a weak stream, no dysuria or hematuria.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 78 kg, BMI 27.6 (obese). Abdomen soft, no suprapubic tenderness. Prostate exam not performed today.
IMPRESSION: Benign prostatic hyperplasia, symptoms mild and stable. Obesity noted.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime and finasteride 5 mg daily. Order PSA and urine routine. Advise reduced fluid intake after 6 pm, regular walks, and weight reduction diet. Return if acute urinary retention, visible blood in urine, fever above 39°C, or severe lower abdominal pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS
Finasteride 5 mg OD

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PSA 4.2 ng/mL (ref 0-4.0). Urine routine: pus cells 2-4/hpf, no bacteria, no blood.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
74-year-old male with BPH returns for symptom review after rising PSA.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nocturia unchanged, weak stream, no new urinary symptoms.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/88 mmHg, weight 77.5 kg, BMI 27.4 (obese). Abdomen soft, no tenderness.
IMPRESSION: BPH stable; PSA mildly elevated at 4.2 ng/mL, likely benign enlargement.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase tamsulosin to 0.4 mg HS twice daily. Keep finasteride 5 mg OD. Repeat PSA in 8 weeks. Advise same lifestyle measures. Return if acute retention, hematuria, fever >39°C, or severe flank pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg BID
Finasteride 5 mg OD

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
74-year-old male with BPH for annual review and influenza vaccination.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nocturia 2-3 times/night, weak stream, no incontinence.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 27.3 (obese). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: BPH stable. Fasting lipid profile: total cholesterol 180 mg/dL, HDL 45, LDL 100, triglycerides 130 (all within target). Fasting blood sugar 92 mg/dL (normal). PSA 4.0 ng/mL (borderline). Obesity persists.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg BID, finasteride 5 mg OD. Influenza vaccine given today 2025-10-20. Advise low‑salt diet, regular aerobic activity, weight loss goal. Return if acute urinary retention, visible blood, fever >39°C, or severe lower abdominal pain.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: TC 180 mg/dL (<200), HDL 45 (>40), LDL 100 (<130), TG 130 (<150). Fasting blood sugar: 92 mg/dL (70-100).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
74-year-old male with BPH reports worsening urinary symptoms.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nocturia 4 times/night, intermittent stream, feeling of incomplete emptying.
EXAMINATION: BP 142/90 mmHg, weight 78 kg, BMI 27.6 (obese). Suprapubic dullness noted.
IMPRESSION: BPH progression suggested by symptoms and mild suprapubic fullness. PSA stable at 4.0 ng/mL.
ARRANGEMENTS: Discontinue finasteride 5 mg OD due to possible decreased libido. Start tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS only. Order repeat PSA and urine routine. Advise pelvic floor exercises, limit caffeine. Return if acute retention, hematuria, fever >39°C, or severe lower abdominal pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
74-year-old male with BPH for follow‑up after stopping finasteride.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nocturia 3 times/night, stream improved but still weak.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/88 mmHg, weight 77.5 kg, BMI 27.4 (obese). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: BPH symptoms moderately improved off finasteride; PSA 4.1 ng/mL unchanged.
ARRANGEMENTS: Restart finasteride 5 mg OD at reduced dose 2.5 mg OD to balance side effects. Continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS. Repeat PSA in 3 months. Advise maintain weight, daily walk. Return if acute retention, hematuria, fever >39°C, or severe flank pain.

Tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS
Finasteride 2.5 mg OD

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
74-year-old male with BPH for routine review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nocturia 2 times/night, good stream, no incontinence.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 76.5 kg, BMI 27.1 (obese). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: BPH well controlled on current regimen. PSA 4.0 ng/mL (stable). Obesity class persists.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS and finasteride 2.5 mg OD. Advise maintain activity, monitor weight. Return if acute retention, hematuria, fever >39°C, or severe lower abdominal pain.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Ultrasound KUB: prostate volume 38 mL, mild bilateral hydronephrosis, post‑void residual 45 mL (normal <50). No calculi.
